newsitem.title: POLAND: High Polish rates soak budget financing reserves.
newsitem.headline: High Polish rates soak budget financing reserves.

text.p: Poland has already exhausted reserves within this year's budget to cover additional outflows stemming from higher finacing costs, the head of the Finance Ministry's public debt department said on Wednesday.
Piotr Dziewulski said high market rates and yields of comparable NBP-bills have pushed up yields on Polish treasuries above expected levels and increased financing costs.

"After five months it is difficult to say...but there should not be any savings on the costs of financing the public deficit this year...as high rates alrady devoured reserves," he told a news conference.
In 1996 Poland had significant savings in financing the budget deficit, which eventually reduced its budget gap to 2.4 percent of the gross domestic product from the planned 2.8 percent of GDP.
"We planned to have yields around 19 percent early in the year and now we have yields at 21 to 21.5 percent depending on the maturity of the paper," he said.
Dziewulski again said that public sales of Polish bonds have been below expectations as many individuals were not interested in purchasing the paper because it was no longer tax-deductible.
He said the non-banking sector's share in financing the budget deficit was satisfactory.
